import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Size, Order, and Connected Domination

*References:*
- [S. Mukwembi, _Size, order, and connected domination_,
  Canad. Math. Bull. 57 (2014), no. 1, 141–144](https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-2013-020-5)
-/

namespace SizeOrderConnectedDomination

open SimpleGraph

/--
**Theorem 2.1** of [S. Mukwembi, _Size, order, and connected domination_,
Canad. Math. Bull. 57 (2014), no. 1, 141–144](https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-2013-020-5)
claims: if $G$ is a connected triangle-free graph of order $n$ and size $m$ with
connected domination number $\gamma_c$, then
$$m \le \frac{(n - \gamma_c)^2}{4} + n - 1.$$

The claim is **false**: the 3-dimensional hypercube $Q_3$ is a counterexample,
with $n = 8$, $m = 12$ and $\gamma_c = 4$, so the asserted bound reads
$12 \le (8-4)^2/4 + 8 - 1 = 11$. The gap in the paper's proof (p. 143) is the
unjustified assertion that there is an edge $uv$ with
$\gamma_c(G) \le \gamma_c(G - \{u, v\})$: in $Q_3$, removing any adjacent pair
of vertices leaves a graph with connected domination number $2 < 4$.

The corollaries of the paper (Corollary 2.2 and 2.3, on leaf numbers of
triangle-free graphs) remain true; Corollary 2.2 is Graffiti.pc Conjecture 1.1,
recorded as `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture2.conjecture2`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/henrykmichalewski/formal-conjectures/blob/238fcea04077aee1d63c9201aa4b4b794f3a674d/FormalConjectures/Paper/SizeOrderConnectedDomination.lean#L156"]
theorem mukwembi_theorem_2_1 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G.Connected → G.CliqueFree 3 →
      (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≤
        ((Fintype.card α : ℝ) - (G.connectedDominationNumber : ℝ)) ^ 2 / 4
          + (Fintype.card α : ℝ) - 1 := by
  sorry

end SizeOrderConnectedDomination

reformulations.difference: Lean assumes Nontrivial α, whereas the paper's Theorem 2.1 does not explicitly exclude the one-vertex connected graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectedness already excludes an empty vertex type. The remaining excluded case has n = 1, m = 0, and connected domination number 1, so the inequality is 0 ≤ 0. Thus the universal inequality with Nontrivial is equivalent to the version without it, and their negative-answer formulations are equivalent as well. Review.domain_equivalence in /workspace/review/verification.lean proves the equivalence of the universal statements without using the imported sorry.

sources_consulted: S. Mukwembi, “Size, Order, and Connected Domination,” Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 57 (2014), 141–144, especially the definitions on p. 141 and Theorem 2.1 and its proof on pp. 142–143: https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-2013-020-5

Full publisher PDF, all four pages: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/777E92AD747F1290046EB18053946CAE/S0008439500007578a.pdf/size-order-and-connected-domination.pdf

Local Mathlib definitions and supporting API: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/{Basic,Finite,Clique,Connectivity/Connected}.lean; Order/Lattice/Nat.lean; Order/ConditionallyCompleteLattice/Basic.lean; Data/Fintype/{Card,EquivFin}.lean.

Local review guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, PROOFS.md. Calibration: past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr01256.md, pr01870.md, pr02208.md, pr04119.md; not_misformalizations/INDEX.md and all eight accompanying cases.
review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully reproduces the inequality in Theorem 2.1 and correctly records its refutation. I independently proved the exact negative-answer statement as Review.negative_answer in /workspace/review/verification.lean: the cube is connected and triangle-free, has 12 edges, and has connected domination number 4, giving the impossible inequality 12 ≤ 11. Its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. I also proved that connectedDominationNumber is attained and lies between 1 and the vertex count under the theorem's hypotheses, ruling out an empty-infimum artifact. Boundary checks cover empty, singleton, and two-vertex graphs. Separate Lean enumeration confirms the docstring's assertion that deleting any adjacent cube vertices leaves connected domination number 2. The GitHub-hosted proof link was not consulted; its mathematical conclusion was independently verified instead.
